utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Defence wanted to raise a preliminary matter. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Thank you. I should like to ask once again, Your Honours, in keeping what you've told us last time, to move again to urgently resolve the issue of the means and pace of work in view of the health of General Mladic. The reason for my address today is that we received yesterday a new report of the medical officer of the Detention Unit, who stands by his previous proposal. And every visit we make to General Mladic also encourages us to ask for this to be solved as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, if the decision will not be signed and filed today, then it will not be later than Monday or Tuesday, if that is sufficient. It also shows that we are working on it very hard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I would like to raise a preliminary scheduling matter about the 92 ter motions in relation to Richard Wright and Christopher Lawrence. On the 1st of July, the Prosecution has filed two urgent Rule 92 ter motions pertaining to Witnesses Wright and Lawrence who are currently scheduled to testify in the week of the 15th of July. On the 4th of July, the Prosecution filed its notice of disclosure of additional expert reports including three reports by Witness Wright. The Prosecution submitted that cognisant of the short notice the Defence has received of the Prosecution's intention to tender these three additional reports by Witness Wright, it is prepared to recall the witness after the summer recess for additional examination, if necessary. On the 10th of July, the Defence filed its response to the motion. In its responses the Defence submits, inter alia, that is inappropriate to introduce extracts from previous testimonies of these witnesses into evidence as the Chamber has not yet reached a conclusion with regard to the overall reliability of Wright and Lawrence as expert witnesses and the statuses of their reports disclosed by the Prosecution on the 6th of November, 2012. In this respect, the Chamber would like to remind the parties of its oral decision of the 24th of May of this year where it considered Witness Wright as an expert in the field of forensic archeology and Witness Lawrence as an expert in the field of forensic pathology. Furthermore, the Chamber deferred its decision of admission into evidence of the tendered reports of these witnesses until the time of their respective testimonies. It is therefore for the Defence to show the alleged unreliability of these witnesses. The Defence further submits that the 92 ter motions were filed less than 30 days before the expected testimony of Witness Wright and Lawrence and is not in compliance with the Chamber's guidance. It also complains about the late filing of the Prosecution's notice containing three additional reports by Witness Wright. As to Witness Lawrence, having reviewed the Defence's submissions and the transcripts tendered by the Prosecution, the Chamber considers that Witness Lawrence can be called to testify in the week of the 15th of July as scheduled. The Chamber further considers that at the end of its cross-examination, the Defence may, if necessary, request that the witness return for further cross-examination. As to Witness Wright, having verified the matter with the Victims and Witness Section, the Chamber notes that the witness was expected to arrive in the Netherlands from Australia early this morning. Consequently, the Chamber considers it to be in the interest of justice that he commences his testimony on Monday, the 15th of July, as scheduled. I immediately add to this that if the Prosecution would examine the witness on the three additional reports, that the Chamber will grant any request by the Defence to have further time to prepare for cross-examination on those three reports. It's very unfortunate that the witness is already on his way because it may result in perhaps a waste of resources - I do not know yet - but therefore we start. The Defence is expected to cross-examine the witness on the reports other than the three new ones. If the Defence would be ready to cross-examine him also on the latest three reports, that's fine. But if the Defence considers that it needs more time to prepare, then the witness will have to be recalled for further cross-examination. Of course, it's also -- the Prosecution could also withdraw the three reports and then, of course, that complication does not arise any further. But we leave that entirely in the hands of the Prosecution. But once examined-in-chief on it, the Defence will have full opportunities to prepare even if that would mean recalling him at a later date. Is this clear to the parties? Then we turn into closed session and will remain for most of the day, if not all of the day, in closed session to hear further testimony of these -- of the present witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I would like to thank, first of all, everyone who assisted in by spending five more minutes to avoid that a witness had to stay here for 72 hours and then remain in Court for a few minutes. Thank you, all, for that. We adjourn for the day and will resume on Monday the 15th of July at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 15th day of July, 2013, at 9.30 a.m. 23 24 25
